summary: ClawSweeper P1 is a real code-level defect: I empirically reproduced it. On a snapshot-only store the post-fix delete path issues TWO saveSnapshot calls (persistTaskDelete projects tasks-without-id, then persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete re-saves the RAW in-memory tasks map which still contains the id because the in-memory delete runs later at L2185) -> the deleted task is resurrected in the persisted snapshot (probe: SAVE CALLS=[{tasks:[]},{tasks:[<id>]}], FINAL=[<id>]). The bot's (b) point is also exact: on the default composite store deleteTaskRecordById calls deleteTaskWithDeliveryState(1) AND then deleteDeliveryState(1) -> a redundant second pre-memory sqlite delivery-state delete (idempotent on success but a real extra write tx). HOWEVER the production hot-path caveat (R-7/CAL-003): the snapshot-only store shape is NOT a production-reachable configuration. The default store (the only production binding) always provides every granular helper, and every other store built in the codebase (test-utils/installInMemoryTaskRegistryRuntime, commands.test-harness) also provides all granular helpers. configureTaskRegistryRuntime has no plugin/external surface. So the resurrection branch the (a) test exercises is real-in-code / synthetic-in-prod, while the (b) atomicity narrowing IS on the real default hot-path. The proposed fix (single atomic delete persist projecting task+delivery once for snapshot-only, composite-only for default; no redundant second pre-memory delete) closes both correctly. Net: real-problem-real-fix, proceed-with-proposed-fix, but the PR must frame (a) as defense-of-the-snapshot-fallback-contract (not a prod incident) and (b) as the prod-hot-path narrowing, else it risks the CAL-003 synthetic-branch trap if claimed as a live production resurrection.

role_specific.production_trigger: Snapshot-only resurrection (bot's primary P1): requires a store with ONLY loadSnapshot+saveSnapshot. No such store is constructed anywhere in src (default + test-utils + test-harness all provide granular delete helpers; configureTaskRegistryRuntime is internal, no plugin surface). The (b) variant (redundant 2nd pre-memory delivery-state delete) DOES trigger on every default-store delete in production: deleteTaskWithDeliveryState removes task+delivery in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE tx, then persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete fires deleteDeliveryState as a second write tx on the already-removed row.
role_specific.branch_taken_in_prod: default composite branch: persistTaskDelete -> store.deleteTaskWithDeliveryState (deleteTaskAndDeliveryStateFromSqlite, withWriteTransaction) returns; persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete -> store.deleteDeliveryState (deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite) returns. Both granular helpers exist so neither saveSnapshot fallback (L302-307 / L330-335) is ever reached in prod. The snapshot fallback branches are dead code for the production store.
required_mocks: configureTaskRegistryRuntime store override (production seam, same seam used by test-utils and prod default binding) — legitimate, not distortion
(a) snapshot-only store = loadSnapshot+saveSnapshot only, NO granular helpers — this shape exists ONLY in test files, so the (a) test exercises a fallback branch that is dead in prod (R-7 caveat)

(b) default-shaped store with deleteTaskWithDeliveryState + deleteDeliveryState as vi.fn() spies, assert deleteDeliveryState NOT called (call count 0) after the composite already removed delivery — this DOES match the prod default branch
role_specific.proposed_tests_assessment: inadequate-as-specified-for-(a), adequate-for-(b). (a) snapshot-only resurrection test: as written it must assert the FINAL persisted snapshot.tasks does NOT contain the deleted id (inspect the LAST saveSnapshot call's snapshot.tasks, not just that saveSnapshot was called) — that exact assertion reproduces the bug (I confirmed RED) and is the right shape. BUT it exercises a snapshot-only store that has no production instantiation, so per R-7 it proves a fallback-contract regression, not a prod incident; PR body must not claim a live production resurrection from it (CAL-003 synthetic-branch risk). (b) narrow assertion: spy deleteDeliveryState with vi.fn and assert toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0) (or that the composite deleteTaskWithDeliveryState is the sole delivery-state delete) IS the correct real-branch assertion and lands on the production default path. Recommend: keep (b) as the real-hot-path regression; keep (a) but label it as snapshot-fallback-contract coverage. For (a) the assertion MUST read snapshot.tasks of the last save (the bug is invisible if you only check has() on a store that re-derives from granular helpers).
new_blocking_problems: Snapshot-fallback inconsistency is the actual root defect, not just delete: persistTaskUpsert (L284-287) and persistTaskDelete (L302-307) project the pending change against the raw in-memory `tasks` map, but persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete (L330-335) and persistTaskDeliveryStateUpsert (L316-319) save the raw `tasks`/`taskDeliveryStates` WITHOUT projecting the sibling pending mutation. Because the persist-before-in-memory fix now runs ALL persist calls BEFORE the in-memory delete, any delete that fans out to two snapshot-fallback persists (delete task + delete delivery) has the SECOND save clobber the FIRST projection. The proposed single-atomic-delete-persist fix resolves this, but the SAME class of bug exists for the upsert path on a snapshot-only store if a delivery-state change and a task change are persisted as two separate fallback saves in one transition (persistTaskUpsert projects task but not the new delivery; a following persistTaskDeliveryStateUpsert saves raw tasks). Verify the fix covers upsert symmetry, not only delete.

Redundant write amplification on prod default store: every deleteTaskRecordById currently runs TWO withWriteTransaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) calls (deleteTaskAndDeliveryState then deleteDeliveryState) for one logical delete — extra lock acquisition under the same SQLITE_BUSY contention the SOL targets. Collapsing to the single composite call (the proposed fix) also reduces this; confirm persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete is skipped when the composite helper already handled delivery.

summary: The underlying SOL-0015 problem (in-memory-before-sqlite ordering causing cross-store divergence) is real and core-reliability-relevant, and the update path is genuinely fixed (persistTaskUpsert at L1013 runs before tasks.set at L1014). But the ClawSweeper P1 is correct against the worktree code: the delete persist path is NOT a single atomic operation. deleteTaskRecordById issues two separate sqlite writes (L2180 persistTaskDelete + L2181 persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete) before touching memory. P1: with the default/composite store, L2180 (deleteTaskAndDeliveryStateFromSqlite, store.sqlite.ts:528) already deletes task AND delivery state in one transaction; L2181 (deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite, store.sqlite.ts:540, a separate non-transactional write) is redundant and, if it throws, leaves sqlite with the task deleted while in-memory still holds it (L2185 not reached) = divergence. P2: with a snapshot-only store, L2180 saves a snapshot with the task projected out, but L2181 (persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete snapshot fallback, L330-335) saves a SECOND snapshot using the live unprojected tasks map (in-memory not yet mutated), re-adding/resurrecting the deleted task. Both bot findings are real. Our proposed fix (collapse to one atomic delete persist: use composite when present and drop the redundant second helper; in snapshot fallback project task+delivery together in one saveSnapshot) closes the gap and does not introduce new divergence. Recommend proceed-with-proposed-fix.

production_impact_scenarios: Default store (production): a task delete during SQLITE_BUSY/IOERR on the redundant second write (persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete -> deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite, store.sqlite.ts:540-542) aborts deleteTaskRecordById after the task is already gone from sqlite (L2180 composite transaction) but before in-memory delete (L2185). sqlite=deleted / in-memory=present until a reload, where reloadTaskRegistryFromStore (task-registry.ts:984) reloads the (now absent) sqlite SoT and silently drops the in-memory record. Cross-store divergence window for any delete that hits contention on the second write.

Snapshot-only store: deleteTaskRecordById persists two snapshots. The first (persistTaskDelete fallback, task-registry.ts:300-307) writes the task projected out; the second (persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete fallback, task-registry.ts:330-335) writes snapshot.tasks = the live `tasks` map, which still contains the deleted task because the in-memory delete at L2185 has not run yet. The second saveSnapshot overwrites the first and resurrects the deleted task in the persisted store -> lost-delete (FIND-001) is re-opened on the delete path even with the current PR.
Either store: even on the success path the delete persist is two sqlite/snapshot writes rather than one, so the delete is non-atomic across the two helpers regardless of which helper fails.
role_specific.maintainer_receptiveness: high - core data-consistency / reliability of task-registry persistence, exactly the memory/reliability area the maintainer guide prioritizes; the fix-shape matches accepted precedent PR #83238 (persist-before-in-memory); PR is XS/S touching only src/tasks (no CODEOWNERS-restricted paths). The follow-up (one atomic delete persist) is a tightening of the same PR, in-scope, one-thing-per-PR safe.
role_specific.reproducibility: moderate - P2 (snapshot-only resurrection) is deterministic and same-process: inject a store with no delete* methods, call deleteTaskRecordById, observe the saved snapshot still contains the task. P1 (composite double-write divergence) needs the second sqlite write (deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite) to throw while the first composite transaction succeeded, reproducible at the store seam by making the deleteDeliveryState method throw while deleteTaskWithDeliveryState succeeds. Both are injectable via configureTaskRegistryRuntime exactly like the existing update test; no disk-full needed.
concerns_acknowledged: The current PR ships only the update-divergence regression test (store.test.ts:234 'does not diverge sqlite-direct reads when an upsert persist throws'); there is NO test covering the delete path's atomicity, snapshot-only resurrection, or the redundant second composite write. The scope-down note in SOL-0015 justified one representative test, but that left the delete-path P1/P2 unguarded - which is precisely what the bot caught.

persistTaskDelete + persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete being two calls is structurally a non-atomic persist; the PR moved both before memory (good for the in-memory<->sqlite boundary) but did not make the two-into-one consolidation the bot demands.
The redundant L2181 call is harmless on the success path with the composite store (delivery already deleted) but is the exact failure surface for P1.
role_specific.proposed_fix_assessment: closes-completely - Removing the redundant persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete when a composite (deleteTaskWithDeliveryState) is bound makes the default-store delete a single atomic transaction (eliminates P1). Collapsing the snapshot fallback so task and delivery-state are projected out together in ONE saveSnapshot (instead of two, the second of which reads the unprojected live tasks map) eliminates the resurrection (P2). Both changes stay within persist-before-in-memory ordering and the existing helper structure, introduce no new index/rollback logic, and do not change store contracts. Two added regression tests (snapshot-only delete does not resurrect; composite delete issues exactly one task+delivery delete with no second pre-memory sqlite write) lock both gaps. No new divergence surface is created.

summary: ClawSweeper P1/P2 are REAL against worktree fc72b62339. The post-fix delete path (deleteTaskRecordById L2180-2181) calls persistTaskDelete THEN a redundant persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete. For the default store, persistTaskDelete binds deleteTaskAndDeliveryStateFromSqlite (store.ts L61) which already deletes task+delivery in ONE withWriteTransaction (sqlite.ts L528-533); the second call deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite (sqlite.ts L540-543) is a non-transactional duplicate DELETE of an already-removed row. If that second write throws AFTER the composite committed, sqlite has the task deleted while in-memory still holds it (in-memory delete is L2185, not yet reached) -> divergence, and on reload loadTaskRegistryStateFromSqlite (sqlite.ts L470-478) the task is GONE while memory keeps it (an asymmetric, opposite-direction inconsistency the PR claims to prevent). For snapshot-only stores P2 is REAL: persistTaskDelete snapshot fallback saves projectedTasks (task removed, L302-305) but persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete snapshot fallback saves the RAW tasks map (L333) which still contains the task, re-adding the just-deleted task by overwriting the correct first snapshot. The PR ships NO delete-divergence regression test (only the upsert test at test L234-308). The current PR persists both delete steps before memory but does not make delete atomic, so the bot's exact failure window survives. Our proposed fix (collapse delete persist to a single atomic op: use composite when present and drop the redundant second call; snapshot-only fallback projects task+delivery in one saveSnapshot) closes the gap, but with a real ordering caveat for capability combos.

hidden_guards_found.evidence_quote: export function deleteTaskRegistryRecordFromSqlite(taskId: string) { const store = openTaskRegistryDatabase(); store.statements.deleteRow.run(taskId); store.statements.deleteDeliveryState.run(taskId); }

export function deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite(taskId: string) { const store = openTaskRegistryDatabase(); store.statements.deleteDeliveryState.run(taskId); }  // second call has NO withWriteTransaction wrapper; runs after composite already committed

role_specific.primary_path_inversion_result: For the bot's P1 to manifest, persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete (the SECOND call, L2181) must throw while persistTaskDelete (FIRST call, L2180) already succeeded+committed. Verified plausible: default store binds the second call to deleteTaskDeliveryStateFromSqlite (sqlite.ts L540-543) which opens the DB via openTaskRegistryDatabase() and runs a single DELETE WITHOUT withWriteTransaction. Same disk-full / SQLITE_IOERR / WAL-write failure modes that the PR cites for the first write apply equally to this second write, and openTaskRegistryDatabase itself can throw. So the persist-before-memory ordering is NOT sufficient: between the two persist calls there is a non-atomic window where sqlite=deleted, memory=present. Inverting the claim does NOT find a guard that prevents it. The composite already removing delivery state means the second call is ENTIRELY redundant work that only adds a failure surface.
cal001_style_misses: The PR self-claims (PR body 'What was not tested') that snapshot-fallback persist branches are 'out of the production path per the FIND counter-evidence' and excludes them, but the snapshot fallback IS reachable for any store configured without the composite/single delete methods, and the bot's P2 shows the new snapshot-fallback code (L328-335) saves the RAW tasks map, actively resurrecting the deleted task. The exclusion masked a defect the PR's own diff introduced.

The post-fix divergence direction for default sqlite is OPPOSITE to the pre-fix one: pre-fix lost-delete = sqlite keeps row -> reload resurrects (task survives); post-fix second-delete-throw = sqlite drops row + memory keeps it -> reload LOSES the row from memory's perspective only after reload (memory stale-present until reload). The PR's regression test and proof only measured the upsert divergence (resurrectedCount via the OLD ordering), never the new delete window, so RED->GREEN never exercised the P1 path.

deleteTaskRegistryRecordFromSqlite (the non-composite deleteTask binding, L522-526) ALSO deletes delivery_state, so the redundant second persist is dead/duplicate work for BOTH default bindings, not just the composite one. Neither bot nor PR notes that the second persist call can be deleted with zero behavior loss on the production path.
role_specific.proposed_fix_assessment: closes-completely — Collapsing the delete persist to a single atomic operation (call only persistTaskDelete which already removes task+delivery via the composite/cascade, and drop the redundant persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete; for snapshot-only fallback, project BOTH task delete and delivery delete in ONE saveSnapshot) eliminates the inter-call non-atomic window (P1) and the raw-tasks-map re-add (P2). Evidence: deleteTaskAndDeliveryStateFromSqlite (L528-533) and deleteTaskRegistryRecordFromSqlite (L522-526) both already delete delivery_state, so removing the second call loses no production behavior. The remaining caveat is the store-capability combos below, which the fix must handle explicitly rather than assuming the composite is always present.
store_capability_combos_at_risk: deleteTask present + deleteTaskWithDeliveryState absent: persistTaskDelete -> store.deleteTask (sqlite.ts default deleteTaskRegistryRecordFromSqlite already cascades delivery, but a custom adapter's deleteTask may delete ONLY the task). Then if the proposed fix drops the second persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete, a custom deleteTask-only store would leak delivery_state. Fix must keep delivery cleanup when the single deleteTask is NOT known to cascade.

deleteTask absent + deleteDeliveryState present (no composite): persistTaskDelete falls through to snapshot fallback (saves projectedTasks) while persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete calls store.deleteDeliveryState. Mixed snapshot+granular path -> two different persistence mechanisms in one logical delete, non-atomic and easy to get wrong under the new ordering.

deleteTaskWithDeliveryState present + deleteDeliveryState absent: current code calls persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete second -> falls through to snapshot fallback (L328-335) which saves the RAW tasks map = re-adds the task even though the composite just deleted it via its own method. This is the exact P2 manifestation and is silently triggered whenever a store has the composite but no granular deleteDeliveryState.
snapshot-only (no composite, no deleteTask, no deleteDeliveryState): both fallbacks fire; second saveSnapshot (L332-335) saves raw tasks -> resurrection (P2 confirmed by reading the diff).
new_blocking_problems: NEW (introduced by this PR's diff, neither in the original FIND nor caught by the bot's headline): the snapshot-fallback in persistTaskDeliveryStateDelete (L328-335) was NOT made consistent with the persist-before-memory ordering for the tasks map — it saves `tasks` raw. Combined with persistTaskDelete's projectedTasks (L302-305), the SECOND snapshot overwrites the FIRST, so for ANY snapshot-only or composite-without-granular store the delete is net-undone. This is a regression the PR itself adds and is blocking for snapshot-backed deployments.

The PR provides zero regression coverage for the delete-divergence path (the only divergence test, test L234-308, is upsert-only). Even after fixing, a delete-throw RED->GREEN test is required to prove the close and prevent re-regression.
